title: Keynote: Why people think "agent" is a buzzword but it isn't
talk_summary: Chip Huyen argues agents aren't hype but are hard: task failure compounds with step count, natural-language-to-API translation is ambiguous on both sides, and context grows fast and degrades in effective length. He gives concrete mitigations: decompose tasks to the model's reliable step budget, document tools exhaustively (errors, return values, interpretation), keep tool sets narrow, ask for clarification when unsure, and use tiered memory (context as short-term, external storage as long-term).

takeaways.evidence_quote: it's very very rare to see them like consistently being to Sol tasks that involve like more than five steps
takeaways.numbers: 2% per-step error over 10 steps ≈ 18% task failure; most models solve ≤5 steps, fail past ~10

takeaways.technique: Exhaustive tool docs incl. error/return interpretation
takeaways.what_they_do: Document each tool's params, types, error codes, expected returns, and how to interpret return values and recover from errors; one company's biggest agent gain came from explaining return-value interpretation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one of the biggest Improvement they got for their agents is after they explained and add to the documentations like how to interpret uh return values

takeaways.what_they_do: Give agents only a few narrow, well-defined tools; a large search company found agents stopped working with more than ~5 tools.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent just did not work at all with like more than five tools
takeaways.numbers: ~3-4 tools worked; >5 failed for that company

takeaways.what_they_do: Distinguish nominal vs effective context (models get 'funky' well before the limit); benchmark where hallucination starts, keep context for task-relevant info, spill step outputs to external files and retrieve on demand.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a model might be able to fit in like a million tokens but like if you give it anything more than like 30,000 tokens it might get really really really funky
takeaways.numbers: anecdotal: degradation observed past ~30k tokens despite 1M-token windows

takeaways.what_they_do: Instruct agents to ask the user when intent is ambiguous rather than guessing (e.g. 'bestselling under $10' — which date range?).
takeaways.evidence_quote: you should definitely instruct your agent to ask for classifications when it's unsure of what users want

takeaways.technique: Match model to task type (planning vs long-context)
takeaways.what_they_do: Observed models strong at planning (output-heavy reasoning) are not necessarily strong at long context (input-heavy), and vice versa; route accordingly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: models that perform well on my long context benchmarks don't perform as well on the planning Benchmark in Vice Vera
